👉 *Living in Molokai | How Life Works Where Hawaii Sees the Fewest Visitors* https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LgYV9P2TlHk
👉Living in Saipan | How Life Works on a US Island Near WWII's Largest Airbase https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m0XCAISNRl8
👉Living in American Samoa | How Life Works Where Some US Laws Don't Apply https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mVZHwtNJifM

On Mayotte, much of the public water network runs on 30 hours of supply, then 42 hours of cuts, and the sources give two kinds of end: the committee ties the cycle to rainfall and reservoir levels, while officials point to new plants, boreholes and a third reservoir by 2032. If you lived here, which stopgap would you want first: more boreholes and plants now, or a bigger reservoir later? And which part of the day would you fix first: the taps, the school shifts, or the one barge across the lagoon? Tell us below, and where you're watching from. 👇
